source.author: verg
source.text: Quod te per caeli iucundum lumen et auras, per genitorem oro, per spes surgentis Iuli, eripe me his, invicte, malis: aut tu mihi terram inice, namque potes, portusque require Velinos; aut tu, si qua via est, si quam tibi diva creatrix ostendit neque enim, credo, sine numine divom flumina tanta paras Stygiamque innare paludem da dextram misero, et tecum me tolle per undas, sedibus ut saltem placidis in morte quiescam.
source.text_original: Quod te per caeli iucundum lumen et auras, / per genitorem oro, per spes surgentis Iuli, / eripe me his, invicte, malis: aut tu mihi terram / inice, namque potes, portusque require Velinos; / aut tu, si qua via est, si quam tibi diva creatrix / ostendit — neque enim, credo, sine numine divom / flumina tanta paras Stygiamque innare paludem — / da dextram misero, et tecum me tolle per undas, / sedibus ut saltem placidis in morte quiescam.
source.text_english: Therefore I beg you, by the sweet light and air of heaven, by my father, by the hopes of rising Iulus, rescue me from these evils, unconquered one: either cast earth upon me, for you can, and seek out the Velinian harbors; or else, if there is any way, if your divine mother has shown you any, for I believe you do not prepare such great rivers and to cross the Stygian marsh without the will of the gods—give your hand to me in my misery, and carry me with you over the waves, so that at least in death I may rest in peaceful abodes.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Phoebe, mone, si Cymaeae mihi conscia vatis stat casta cortina domo, si laurea digna fronte viret; tuque o, pelagi cui maior aperti fama, Caledonius postquam tua carbasa vexit Oceanus Phrygios prius indignatus Iulos, eripe me populis et habenti nubila terrae, sancte pater, veterumque fave veneranda canenti facta virum.
reuse.text_original: Phoebe, mone, si Cymaeae mihi conscia vatis / stat casta cortina domo, si laurea digna / fronte viret; tuque o, pelagi cui maior aperti / fama, Caledonius postquam tua carbasa vexit / Oceanus Phrygios prius indignatus Iulos, / eripe me populis et habenti nubila terrae, / sancte pater, veterumque fave veneranda canenti / facta virum.
reuse.text_english: Phoebus, give me guidance, if the chaste tripod of the Cumaean prophetess stands as a witness in my house, if the laurel grows green on a brow worthy of it; and you, whose fame is greater over the open sea, since Caledonian Ocean bore your sails after, in anger, it had first borne the Phrygian Iulii, rescue me from the peoples and from the earth that holds the clouds, holy father, and favor the ancient deeds of men, while I sing them in reverence.
